tasks.short: Determine the software, hardware and capacity needed for a proposed system change.

steps.what: Clarify workloads, user needs and service constraints with the business lead.
Inspect asset records and infrastructure management consoles for capacity and compatibility.
Read technical manuals and support terms to identify configuration constraints.

loop.input: Versioned manuals, support terms and the system inventory.
loop.output: Draft constraints with source passages, versions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each constraint; analyst verifies critical compatibility and support limits.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting material goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Compatibility conditions appear in varied prose and tables. Fixed rules handle known fields only.

steps.what: Calculate sizing, licence quantities and indicative costs in a comparison workbook.
Choose a configuration and document assumptions, alternatives and unresolved risks.
Approve the resource specification or return it for revision.

tasks.design: A read-only integration brings asset and capacity records from the {HELPDESK} and infrastructure management tools in {OTHER} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop prepares cited constraints from the {DOCS}; deterministic calculations generate sizing scenarios and a draft resource specification. The analyst chooses the configuration, and the IT manager approves its use in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory, support conditions and sizing assumptions sit in separate places. Maintaining their mappings often costs more than preparing an occasional specification.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, calculators and templates. Bounded document extraction can assist with prose; neither removes the need to verify assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete inventories, uncertain demand, licence interpretation and unusual dependencies. Access and employee consultation can take longer where infrastructure data exposes staff activity.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which service risks and capacity margins are acceptable when demand and business priorities conflict.

ambition.what: Quarterly capacity headroom decisions for order processing.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing demand scenarios and resolving service trade-offs. Approval and spending rights do not change.

reach.task: Translate seasonal order volumes into system capacity scenarios.
reach.learn: Peak arrival patterns, operational bottlenecks and the cost of delayed processing.

reach.task: Turn the resource specification into a phased implementation estimate.
reach.learn: Delivery dependencies, lead times and contingency planning.

evidence.claim: Inventory integration, sizing calculators and specification templates are feasible with conventional software.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrate prompted document extraction; Microsoft warns that extracted values can be wrong.
Developer field trials found productivity gains, but do not establish a 10-to-100-fold speedup for this solution.

assumptions: Ranges estimate a pilot for one system family with usable exports or read APIs.
The system inventory contains configuration and aggregate capacity data, rather than individual productivity measures.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the actual data and use. Consultation follows national rules.
The time split retains substantial human discussion and configuration judgement, consistent with the task priors.
unknowns: Inventory completeness and available read access.
Whether existing configured reports already cover the required inventory and sizing.
Approved demand forecasts, service targets and licence interpretations.
Whether national consultation requirements apply to the proposed data collection.
Who may approve resource specifications and capacity trials.
research_questions: Which sizing rules can be tested against previous changes and observed capacity?
How often do extracted compatibility conditions omit an important version limitation?
Does an existing inventory report make a new connector unnecessary?
new_work: Verify critical extracted constraints and resolve conflicting manuals.
Maintain inventory mappings, sizing formulas and price dates.
Investigate stale or missing capacity data.
Compare predicted capacity with observed results after implementation.

tasks.short: Read technical material and test examples to learn how to meet user requirements.

steps.what: Turn a user requirement or knowledge gap into specific technical questions.
Find relevant manuals, technical reports and articles in documentation portals and document stores.
Read selected sources and identify relevant techniques, limitations and examples.

loop.input: Retrieved passages from the approved source set and specific technical questions.
loop.output: A short findings draft with exact citations, version limits and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check that citations resolve and passages support each claim; analyst reads decisive passages in context.
loop.stop: One answer and one correction pass per question; unsupported questions return source links without an answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search retrieves passages, but relating varied technical explanations to a particular requirement needs language interpretation.

steps.what: Try documented examples in a development sandbox and assess their fit.
Record useful findings, source versions and cautions for later design work.

tasks.design: Configure version-aware search over an approved source catalogue in the {DOCS}, including links to technical documentation portals in {OTHER}. A bounded reading loop returns cited findings, and a deterministic template assembles source versions and sandbox results into reusable notes. The analyst checks decisive passages, tries examples and approves shared findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Search returns documents rather than a checked answer to a specific implementation question. Source versions and local requirements are difficult to keep aligned.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval, citation checks and document templates are established techniques. A bounded model loop can now reduce initial reading and note preparation, subject to source verification.
tasks.still_hard: Learning enough to notice a misleading answer still takes practice. Restricted manuals, conflicting versions and undocumented behaviour limit coverage.
tasks.human_edge: Build an accurate mental model, recognise missing context and test whether a technique actually fits the requirement.

ambition.what: Version-change impact briefs for project managers.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time locating passages and more time experimenting and explaining consequences. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess how a platform version change affects the delivery plan.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, schedule uncertainty and how to express technical findings as delivery consequences.

reach.task: Check whether documented recovery methods work in a representative sandbox.
reach.learn: Recovery objectives, restoration evidence and operational dependencies.

evidence.claim: Configured search, source version records and deterministic note templates can support technical research.
A bounded reading loop can draft cited findings, but citation presence alone does not establish technical correctness.
METR's early developer study found slower work with AI; its later update describes uncertainty, supporting local measurement.
The later METR update does not establish a settled productivity estimate for current tools.

assumptions: The pilot covers a bounded set of technical topics and approved sources.
The analyst continues to read important original passages; summaries do not replace hands-on learning.
Sandbox examples use synthetic or approved sample data.
GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are checked for the selected processing. Access and consultation follow national rules.
Reading remains the largest activity, as suggested by the priors.
unknowns: Rights to index or process licensed manuals and technical reports.
Which versions are actually deployed.
Availability of an isolated development sandbox.
Whether current search can already filter by version and permissions.
Required consultation for indexing internal documents.
research_questions: Can analysts answer representative questions faster without losing understanding?
How often do answers cite a correct passage from the wrong version?
Which topics should return sources only because synthesis is unreliable?
new_work: Maintain the approved source catalogue and version labels.
Review unsupported answers and misleading citations.
Retire findings when their source versions become obsolete.
Maintain representative questions and sandbox examples for evaluation.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain system design procedures, test procedures and quality standards.

steps.what: Read existing procedures, design records, defects and audit findings.
Agree acceptance criteria, risk tolerances and required evidence with delivery and quality leads.
Draft or revise design procedures, test instructions and quality standards.

loop.input: Approved quality criteria, existing sections and relevant design evidence.
loop.output: A sectioned procedure draft with traceable changes and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections and references; analyst checks changed instructions against design evidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per section; unresolved policy or design questions remain explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but adapting instructions to changed designs requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Write test cases and scripts in test-management and source-repository tools.

loop.input: Acceptance criteria, interface definitions, test templates and approved sample data.
loop.output: Draft test cases and scripts linked to acceptance criteria.
loop.check: Check syntax, scan code and run in isolation; analyst checks assertions and missing failure cases.
loop.stop: One generation and two repair attempts per routine; remaining failures return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable tests use templates. New application behaviours require contextual translation into checks and assertions.

steps.what: Run test routines in a test runner and retain results.
Review coverage and approve the procedure pack or request changes.
Publish the approved revision and update procedure links.

tasks.design: Configure linked evidence views in the {PROJECT} and versioned templates in the {DOCS}. Bounded loops draft changed procedure sections and new test routines; a configured test runner in {OTHER} executes checks in isolation and retains results. Approval by the quality lead triggers publication and link updates through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures, design evidence and tests drift apart. Templates reduce formatting work but cannot decide which controls a changed system needs.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes generators and traceability checks cheaper to build. Bounded drafting can handle changed prose and test code while existing runners perform deterministic validation.
tasks.still_hard: Good assertions, representative test data and coverage of failure modes. Passing generated tests can hide a shared misunderstanding of the requirement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful quality thresholds and challenge whether the evidence would reveal a serious failure.

ambition.what: Release-readiness packs for small operations teams without dedicated quality staff.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time designing failure scenarios and coaching delivery teams. Authority to approve standards remains with the quality lead.

reach.task: Translate operational failure modes into acceptance criteria and evidence requirements.
reach.learn: Risk-based sampling, control effectiveness and defect escape analysis.

reach.task: Add recovery and degraded-service checks to release readiness.
reach.learn: Recovery dependencies, exercise design and evidence of successful restoration.

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents generate test plans and tests and repair failures; this supports test drafting capability, not reliable coverage.
GitHub Copilot offers coding and review assistance with human oversight.
The cited Veracode tests found substantial security problems in generated code, supporting independent checks of test helpers and scripts.
Versioned templates, approval-triggered publication and deterministic traceability checks are conventional implementations.

assumptions: Ranges cover one application, one procedure family and an existing isolated test environment.
Established test runners and document approval features are configured before adding custom code.
The quality lead has authority to approve the procedure pack.
Generated routines have no production credentials.
GDPR applies to personal data in test evidence. EU AI Act requirements and consultation under national rules are assessed for the actual use.
Creation remains central, but structured execution and publication are more automatable than the judgement-heavy priors suggest.
unknowns: Available test infrastructure and existing document approval features.
Whether requirements have usable acceptance criteria.
Test-data sensitivity and permission to create representative samples.
Who approves standards and exceptions.
Whether evidence collection changes employee monitoring and requires consultation.
research_questions: Do generated tests detect deliberately introduced faults?
Which procedure sections can be rendered entirely from structured design records?
What proportion of maintenance effort comes from changing interfaces rather than drafting?
new_work: Review changed instructions and generated assertions.
Maintain templates, traceability rules and isolated test environments.
Investigate flaky tests and unexplained coverage gaps.
Check that publication uses the exact approved revision.
Retire obsolete procedures and test routines.

tasks.short: Compare equipment or software options and recommend a justified choice.

steps.what: Agree evaluation criteria, budget assumptions and adoption constraints with the business sponsor.
Read supplier proposals, specifications and commercial terms against the criteria.

loop.input: Received proposals, specifications, commercial terms and evaluation criteria.
loop.output: A cited fact table separating quoted facts, supplier claims and missing answers.
loop.check: Validate currencies, dates and units; analyst checks material price, support, security and exit conditions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; ambiguity remains flagged for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposal formats and contractual wording vary. Fixed parsers handle standard fields but miss qualified claims.

steps.what: Calculate comparable costs and score evidenced features in an evaluation workbook.
Discuss trial results, practical fit and adoption trade-offs with service owners.
Choose a preferred option and explain trade-offs, risks and implementation conditions.
Endorse the preferred option or request further evidence.

tasks.design: Use the {PROCUREMENT} and {DOCS} as the proposal record, with a bounded extraction loop preparing cited comparison facts. Deterministic calculations produce cost scenarios, an options matrix and a recommendation template from agreed criteria. The analyst judges fit with service owners, and sponsor endorsement in the {PROJECT} hands the recommendation to procurement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Infrequent evaluations use inconsistent proposals and one-off comparison workbooks. Normalising facts helps, but cannot settle conflicting priorities or adoption risks.
tasks.enabler_now: Small extraction and comparison tools are cheaper to build and adapt. Existing records and approval features can carry the workflow without an autonomous purchasing agent.
tasks.still_hard: Testing supplier claims, estimating migration and exit costs, and judging operational fit. Supplier clarification and contract review can dominate elapsed time.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge attractive claims, weigh organisational readiness and explain a recommendation that stakeholders can defend.

ambition.what: Software exit-readiness assessments for departmental system owners.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time on trials, migration risks and stakeholder decisions. Recommendation, purchasing and contract-signing rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess how a proposed system changes administrative workloads and service access.
reach.learn: Frontline work patterns, accessibility needs and adoption costs.

reach.task: Compare the expected operational benefit with migration and exit costs.
reach.learn: Benefits measurement, sensitivity analysis and process-change evaluation.

evidence.claim: Structured comparison tables, cost calculators and recommendation templates can be built with deterministic software.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrate extraction from documents, with explicit warnings about incorrect values.
The digest provides no documented case showing that an automated recommendation makes better equipment or software choices.

assumptions: Ranges cover one evaluation framework and a small set of received proposals.
The tool uses approved evaluation weights and leaves unknown facts unscored.
Sponsor endorsement is a preferred-option decision, not a purchase order or signed contract.
GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the proposed use. Employee consultation follows national rules where system adoption affects staff.
Judgement and discussion remain the majority of human work, consistent with the priors.
unknowns: Available proposal records and rights to process confidential supplier material.
Whether an existing configured evaluation module already meets the need.
Approved cost horizon, scoring rules and budget assumptions.
Quality of trial evidence and access to representative users.
Applicable consultation requirements and procurement approval thresholds.
research_questions: Which proposal fields can be required in a structured submission instead of extracted?
How sensitive is the preferred option to uncertain migration, support and exit costs?
Does the comparison distinguish verified capabilities from supplier claims reliably?
new_work: Review material extracted terms and request missing evidence.
Maintain cost assumptions, scoring formulas and evaluation templates.
Record why human judgement differs from the calculated ranking.
Check realised costs and adoption outcomes against the recommendation.
Update exit-readiness assessments when contracts or dependencies change.

role.altitude: The systems analyst spends less time assembling evidence and formatting records, and more time testing assumptions, designing controls and resolving operational trade-offs. Formal spending, standards and production-change authority remains with the existing approvers.
reach: Connect capacity planning with logistics analysts' demand scenarios.
Turn technical findings into delivery consequences with project management specialists.
Develop recovery evidence with business continuity planners.
Test operational benefits and exit costs with management analysts.
skills_to_grow: Design deterministic calculators, templates and integration checks.
Evaluate extraction accuracy and source-version correctness.
Write acceptance criteria and tests that reveal meaningful failures.
Run cost and capacity sensitivity analysis.
Facilitate decisions across technical and operational roles.
Apply data minimisation, access controls and consultation requirements to the actual use.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring system decision service: capacity headroom reviews, version-change impact briefs, release-readiness packs and exit-readiness assessments. Seek an explicit mandate to approve bounded non-production trials, supported by evidence and agreed limits.
